title: Lists
summary: Write bulleted, numbered, nested and description lists.

quiz.q: Which element should you use for the **steps** of a recipe?
quiz.explain: Steps have an order, so use an ordered list. `<li>` is an item, not a list.

quiz.q: Fill in the element for a single list item.
quiz.explain: Each item in `ul` or `ol` is an `<li>`.

quiz.q: In a description list, which element holds the **meaning** of a term?
quiz.explain: `dt` is the term, `dd` is the description, and `dl` wraps the whole list.

quiz.q: Click the line that breaks the rules for a list.
quiz.explain:
Only `
  • ` may be a direct child of `
      `. Change the paragraph to `
    • Coffee
      • `.

exercise.task:
Build four lists in `index.html`.

- A `<ul>` with at least 3 items.
- An `<ol>` with at least 3 items.
- One item that contains a nested list (a `ul` or `ol` inside an `li`).
- A `<dl>` with at least 2 `dt` terms, each followed by a `dd`.
hints: Start with the ul and ol, and give each three li items.
For a nested list, do not close the li yet. Put a new ul inside it, then close the li. For dl, alternate dt and dd.

checks.name: A ul has at least 3 items
An ol has at least 3 items
A list is nested inside a list item
A dl has at least 2 terms (dt)
A dl has at least 2 descriptions (dd)
